title: Adjoining exterior and divided-power variables to a graded divided-power algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}A_i$ be a nonnegative strictly graded commutative unital $R$-algebra [def-sfb-nonnegative-strict-graded-algebra] with a graded divided-power structure $\gamma$ [def-sfb-graded-divided-power-structure], and let $e>0$ be an integer. (1) Odd variable. Let $e$ be odd and put $A\langle T\rangle=A\oplus AT$, a free left $A$-module on $1,T$, graded by $A\langle T\rangle_m=A_m\oplus A_{m-e}T$, with the $R$-bilinear multiplication $(a+bT)(c+b'T)=ac+(ab'+(-1)^{j}bc)T$ for $a,b,b'\in A$ and homogeneous $c\in A_j$ (so $T^2=0$ and $Tc=(-1)^jcT$). Then $A\langle T\rangle$ is a nonnegative strictly graded commutative unital $R$-algebra containing $A$ as a graded subalgebra, and there is exactly one graded divided-power structure on $A\langle T\rangle$ restricting to $\gamma$ on $A_{\mathrm{even},+}$; it is $\gamma_n(x+yT)=\gamma_n(x)+\gamma_{n-1}(x)yT$ for $n>0$, $x\in A_{\mathrm{even},+}$ and $y\in A_{\mathrm{odd}}$. (2) Even variable. Let $e$ be even and put $A\langle T\rangle=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}AT^{[a]}$, a free left $A$-module on symbols $T^{[a]}$ of degree $ae$, graded by $A\langle T\rangle_m=\bigoplus_{a\geq0}A_{m-ae}T^{[a]}$, with the $R$-bilinear multiplication $(bT^{[a]})(cT^{[a']})=\binom{a+a'}{a}bc\,T^{[a+a']}$ for $b,c\in A$; write $T^{[0]}=1$ and $T=T^{[1]}$. Then $A\langle T\rangle$ is a nonnegative strictly graded commutative unital $R$-algebra containing $A$ as a graded subalgebra, and there is exactly one graded divided-power structure on $A\langle T\rangle$ restricting to $\gamma$ on $A_{\mathrm{even},+}$ with $\gamma_a(T)=T^{[a]}$ for all $a\geq1$. It satisfies $\gamma_n(T^{[a]})=\frac{(na)!}{n!(a!)^n}T^{[na]}$ for $n,a\geq1$ (an integer coefficient acting by repeated addition) and $\gamma_n(bT^{[a]})=\frac{(na)!}{n!(a!)^n}b^nT^{[na]}$ for $b\in A_{\mathrm{even}}$, $a\geq1$. (3) Sets of variables. For a set $J$ and a fixed degree $e>0$, let $A\langle T_j:j\in J\rangle$ be the directed union, over the finite subsets $S\subseteq J$, of the algebras obtained from $A$ by adjoining the $T_j$, $j\in S$, one at a time as in (1) or (2) (for different orders of adjunction these are identified by the unique isomorphisms of graded $R$-algebras that preserve divided powers, are the identity on $A$ and fix every $T_j$ (hence fix every $T_j^{[a]}$ when $e$ is even)). It is a nonnegative strictly graded commutative unital $R$-algebra with exactly one graded divided-power structure restricting to $\gamma$ on $A$ and, for even $e$, with $\gamma_a(T_j)=T_j^{[a]}$ for all $j$ and $a\geq1$. (4) Unions. If $A=A^{(0)}\subseteq A^{(1)}\subseteq A^{(2)}\subseteq\cdots$ are graded subalgebras, each $A^{(k+1)}$ obtained from $A^{(k)}$ as in (3) with its extended divided powers, then $\bigcup_kA^{(k)}$, with the union grading, is a nonnegative strictly graded commutative unital $R$-algebra with exactly one graded divided-power structure restricting to the given one on every $A^{(k)}$.

proof.text: Write $C=A_{\mathrm{even}}$, $I=A_{\mathrm{even},+}$ and $O=A_{\mathrm{odd}}$. The strict graded-commutativity axioms make $C$ a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal, and $O$ a $C$-module. The five ordinary divided-power axioms on $(C,I)$ are exactly the corresponding axioms of the given graded structure, with $\gamma_0=1$. Thus the ordinary extension lemmas apply without assuming that the whole algebra $A$ is commutative.

For odd $e$, let $\sigma$ act by $(-1)^i$ on $A_i$. It is an algebra involution. On pairs representing $a+bT$, multiplication is $(a,b)(c,d)=(ac,ad+b\sigma(c))$. Expanding either association of three factors gives $(acf,acg+ad\sigma(f)+b\sigma(c)\sigma(f))$, so the product is associative and $(1,0)$ is a unit. The indicated degrees add. For homogeneous inputs, moving $T$ past a coefficient gives precisely the graded sign; hence the product is graded commutative. A homogeneous odd element has $a$ odd and $b$ even, and its square is $a^2+(ab-ba)T=0$. The inclusion $a\mapsto(a,0)$ is injective and graded.

The even ring of this odd-variable algebra is $C\oplus OT$, with square-zero ideal $OT$, and its positive-even ideal is $I\oplus OT$. Apply the split square-zero lemma with $M=OT$. It gives the ordinary structure $\delta_n(x+yT)=\gamma_n(x)+\gamma_{n-1}(x)yT$. If $x+yT$ is homogeneous of degree $m>0$, both summands have degree $nm$, so this structure preserves degrees.

To verify the extra odd-product axiom, take as generators of the odd part over its even ring all homogeneous odd elements of $A$, together with $T$. For two old generators the required vanishing is the given axiom on $A$. For an old generator and $T$ it is the square-zero lemma, and for $(T,T)$ it follows from $T^2=0$ and $\delta_n(0)=0$. This generator check implies the axiom for arbitrary odd products by the following explicit two expansions. For a fixed odd generator $s$, expand $v=\sum c_jt_j$ with even $c_j$: higher divided powers of each $c_jst_j$ vanish, and any two of these terms multiply to zero since they share $s$ and $s^2=0$. The addition formula gives $\delta_n(sv)=0$ for $n>1$. Next expand $u=\sum d_is_i$: the same argument applies to $d_is_iv$, since every two terms share $v$ and $v^2=0$. Here every odd $v$, even inhomogeneous, squares to zero: its homogeneous component squares vanish and its cross terms cancel in pairs. For uniqueness, any graded extension must vanish for $n>1$ on every $y_iT$ with $y_i$ homogeneous odd. Such summands multiply to zero, so the addition formula forces vanishing on every $yT$; the same formula then forces the displayed value on $x+yT$.

For even $e$, the basis symbols are central. On three basis elements associativity follows from $\binom{a+b}{a}\binom{a+b+c}{a+b}=(a+b+c)!/(a!b!c!)=\binom{b+c}{b}\binom{a+b+c}{a}$, an identity of integers. This proves associativity after extension by distributivity; $T^{[0]}$ is the unit. Degrees add and the sign is the sign of the coefficients, so graded commutativity holds. In the square of a homogeneous odd sum $\sum b_aT^{[a]}$, each $b_a$ is odd: diagonal terms vanish by $b_a^2=0$ and terms with distinct indices cancel in pairs. Thus the algebra is strictly graded commutative and contains $A$ injectively.

Its even ring is the ordinary divided-power polynomial algebra $C\langle T\rangle$, and its positive-even ideal is $IC\langle T\rangle+C\langle T\rangle_+$. Apply the ordinary polynomial-extension lemma with one variable. The iterate axiom forces $\delta_n(T^{[a]})=(na)!/(n!(a!)^n)T^{[na]}$, and the scalar axiom gives the asserted formula for $bT^{[a]}$. For $z=x_0+\sum_{a>0}x_aT^{[a]}$ its addition formula expands $\delta_n(z)$ into terms $\gamma_{k_0}(x_0)\prod_{a>0}\delta_{k_a}(x_aT^{[a]})$ with $\sum k_a=n$, taking zeroth factors as 1. If $z$ is homogeneous of degree $m$, each such factor has degree $k_am$ (and the constant factor degree $k_0m$). Consequently every term has degree $nm$.

proof.text: The homogeneous odd elements of $A$ generate the odd part of the even-variable algebra over its even ring, since $\sum u_aT^{[a]}$ has odd coefficients $u_a$. On each pair of these generators the extended divided powers agree with those on $A$, which vanish for $n>1$. To pass from pairs of these generators to arbitrary odd elements, first expand $v=\sum c_jt_j$ for fixed generator $s$: each $c_jst_j$ has zero higher divided powers by the scalar axiom, and all products of two terms are zero because $s^2=0$. The addition formula gives $\delta_n(sv)=0$ for $n>1$. Expanding $u=\sum d_is_i$ gives the same conclusion for $uv$, since products of two $d_is_iv$ vanish by $v^2=0$. The latter identity holds for every odd $v$ by cancellation of homogeneous cross terms. This proves the extra graded axiom. Any graded extension restricts to an ordinary divided-power structure on exactly the ideal in the preceding step, fixes the given structure on $I$, and sends $T$ to its prescribed divided powers; ordinary uniqueness proves graded uniqueness.

Induct on the number of variables in a finite set $S$: the empty set gives $A$, and adjoining one further variable is the construction already proved, so every ordering gives the required structure. Comparisons are explicit: move each odd $T_j$ to the target symbol and use its square-zero relation and graded signs; for even variables move $T_j^{[a]}$ to the target $\gamma_a(T_j)$. The odd relations and the binomial multiplication identity for divided powers prove that these maps respect products. At each adjunction, the odd formula or the finite-sum expansion in step 6 proves that they preserve divided powers. The reverse assignment is inverse, since the maps fix the coefficient algebra and every basis monomial. A map preserving divided powers and fixing $T_j$ fixes every divided symbol, so these maps are unique. Thus comparisons compose coherently. The inclusions for $S\subset S\cup\{j\}$ are injective because they include precisely the basis monomials with exponent zero in $T_j$.

source.place: Tag 0F4I, remark-adjoining-set-of-variables; repeated application of 09PH/09PI and their formulas

proof.text: For any set $J$, use these coherent inclusions to identify the finite algebras inside the free $A$-module on finite-support variable monomials (exponents 0 or 1 in the odd case). Any two finite supports are contained in their finite union. Therefore addition, multiplication and divided powers on an element are computed in any finite algebra containing its support, independently of that choice. Every algebra identity and every divided-power axiom has finitely many inputs, so it holds in one such finite algebra. A homogeneous input has the same degree there, proving the grading axiom. A putative extending structure restricts on each finite algebra to the unique structure already proved, giving uniqueness on the union.

source.place: Tag 0F4I, directed union over finite subsets; explicit finite-support argument

proof.text: For the increasing sequence in (4), define each operation on an element using any $A^{(k)}$ containing it. The inclusions preserve all the operations, so this does not depend on $k$. Finitely many inputs belong to one stage (take the largest index); every algebra and divided-power identity follows there. The inclusions preserve the grading, so a finite sum of components which is zero already vanishes in one stage, where each component is zero. Thus the union grading is a direct sum, remains nonnegative, and has the asserted degrees. Finally any structure restricting to all stages agrees on every element with these operations, proving uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem odd_variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : AlgebraData.{u, v} R) (γ : GradedDividedPowers A.grade) (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e) (heodd : Odd e) : ∃ (B : AlgebraData.{u, v} R) (p : OddPresentation A B e) (δ : GradedDividedPowers B.grade), Preserves p.inclusion γ δ ∧ (∀ δ' : GradedDividedPowers B.grade, Preserves p.inclusion γ δ' → δ' = δ) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : evenSubalgebra A.grade) (y : A.Carrier) (z : evenSubalgebra B.grade), 0 < n → x ∈ positiveEvenIdeal A.grade → y ∈ oddPart A.grade → (z : B.Carrier) = p.coordinates.symm ((x : A.Carrier), y) → (δ.dpow n z : B.Carrier) = p.coordinates.symm ((γ.dpow n x : A.Carrier), (γ.dpow (n - 1) x : A.Carrier) * y)
